title: Galacturonic Acid Alleviates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Macrophage Inflammation Potentially Through Competitively Inhibiting the TLR4/NF-kappaB Pathway.
authors: Li, Yan; Ling, Chong; Fang, Jiarong; Ye, Hui; Cao, Qingyun; Feng, Dingyuan; Zhang, Changming; Dong, Zemin; Zuo, Jianjun; Wang, Weiwei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究半乳糖醛酸对LPS诱导巨噬细胞炎症的缓解作用，涉及TLR4/NF-kB通路和分子对接，但对象为小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: d-Galacturonic acid (GA) is a primary component of pectins that spread widely in multifarious plant-derived foods. However, studies on the bioactivity of GA are relatively limited. This study aimed at investigating the anti-inflammatory properties of GA on inflammatory damages induced by lipopolysaccharide (LPS) in RAW264.7 macrophages. The results demonstrated that GA not only alleviated the LPS-induced sharp increase in the mRNA expression of various inflammatory factors but also suppressed LPS-induced activation of the Toll-like receptor (TLR)4/NF-kappaB pathway by decreasing the protein expression levels of TLR4, Phospho (P)-p65, and P-IkappaB-alpha in macrophages. Furthermore, we found that the above effects of GA depended on the TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway by pre-treating macrophages with specific inhibitors targeting TLR4 and p65. Molecular docking analysis identified a potential binding interaction between GA and CD14 (an accessory protein contributing to the recognition of LPS by TLR4). Finally, we found that treating macrophages with GA alone increased the expression of CD14 and TLR4 along with several inflammatory cytokines in macrophages, but the increased amplitude was relatively low. In conclusion, GA can mildly activate the immune responses in macrophages potentially by binding to CD14, but it is capable of competitively inhibiting the binding of LPS to CD14, thereby mitigating LPS-induced inflammation via TLR4/NF-kappaB pathway in macrophages. PRACTICAL APPLICATIONS: This study suggests that galacturonic acid (GA, a monosaccharide present in pectin) exhibits notable anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic properties. It is expected that the intake of GA or other GA-rich substances will enhance the body's immunity.
abstract_zh: d-半乳糖醛酸（GA）是果胶的主要成分，广泛存在于多种植物源性食品中。然而，关于GA生物活性的研究相对有限。本研究旨在探讨GA对脂多糖（LPS）诱导的RAW264.7巨噬细胞炎症损伤的抗炎作用。结果表明，GA不仅能缓解LPS诱导的多种炎症因子mRNA表达的急剧增加，还通过降低巨噬细胞中Toll样受体（TLR）4、磷酸化（P）-p65和P-IκB-α的蛋白表达水平，抑制了LPS诱导的TLR4/NF-κB通路激活。此外，通过使用靶向TLR4和p65的特异性抑制剂预处理巨噬细胞，我们发现GA的上述效应依赖于TLR4/NF-κB通路。分子对接分析确定了GA与CD14（一种有助于TLR4识别LPS的辅助蛋白）之间潜在的结合相互作用。最后，我们发现单独用GA处理巨噬细胞会增加CD14和TLR4以及若干炎症因子的表达，但增加的幅度相对较低。总之，GA可能通过结合CD14温和激活巨噬细胞的免疫反应，但能够竞争性抑制LPS与CD14的结合，从而通过TLR4/NF-κB通路减轻LPS诱导的巨噬细胞炎症。实际应用：本研究表明，半乳糖醛酸（GA，果胶中的一种单糖）具有显著的抗炎和抗凋亡特性。预期摄入GA或其他富含GA的物质将增强机体免疫力。
